description: Declarative DSH adaptations of the vendored BaseMind skills. scripts/sync-basemind-skills.mjs applies every rule to the named upstream file; a rule that matches a different number of times than expectOccurrences fails the sync (that is the drift detector for upstream rewording). Edit this file, then re-run `node scripts/sync-basemind-skills.mjs --tag v0.34.0`; never hand-edit skills/**.

rules.find:
The plugin runs its own version-matched binary, so launch the CLI through it:
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/mcp-launch.sh <args>` (in other hosts, `scripts/mcp-launch.sh` in the
plugin directory). Bare `basemind` from `PATH` is the fallback when no plugin launcher exists; a
different version there shares the same cache. Examples below write `basemind` for brevity.
rules.replace:
The plugin runs its own version-matched binary, so launch the CLI through it: call the
`mcp__basemind__cli` tool with `args: ["code", "grep", …]` — the plugin runs the same verified
binary as the MCP tools (no shell, argv only), so `basemind code grep …` and the MCP server share
the same cache. Bare `basemind` from `PATH` is only a fallback when the plugin is disabled; a
different version there shares the same cache. Examples below write `basemind` for brevity.

rules.find:

`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/mcp-launch.sh <args>` (in other hosts, `scripts/mcp-launch.sh` in the
plugin directory); use bare `basemind` from `PATH` only when no plugin launcher exists.
rules.replace:
Run the `basemind …` commands below through the plugin-managed, version-matched binary: call the
`mcp__basemind__cli` tool with `args: ["doctor"]` or `args: ["status"]` — the plugin runs the same
verified binary as the MCP tools (no shell, argv only), so the CLI and the MCP server share one
cache. Use bare `basemind` from `PATH` only when the plugin is disabled.

rules.find:
1. The plugin launcher, which installs and execs the version-matched binary:
   `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/mcp-launch.sh scan` (in other hosts, `scripts/mcp-launch.sh` in the
   plugin directory). Its binary is cached at `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/basemind/versions/<version>/basemind`.
2. Fallback when no plugin launcher exists: `basemind` on `PATH`.
rules.replace:
1. The plugin's version-matched binary. In DSH the `mcp__basemind__cli` tool runs it (the same
   verified binary as the MCP tools, no shell, argv only; cached at
   `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/basemind/versions/<version>/basemind`), but `scan` is a write verb
   that stays blocked there: use the `index_rescan` MCP tool instead, or run `basemind scan`
   yourself in a terminal.
2. Fallback when no plugin launcher exists: `basemind` on `PATH`.

rules.find:
The MCP server is launched by the host (`basemind serve`, wired up in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
for you). You do not start it manually.

The MCP server is launched by the `dsh-basemind-plugin` bundle (`basemind serve`, wired up in the

rules.find: - **Cursor / others**: toggle/reconnect the basemind MCP server in the MCP settings.
rules.replace:
- **Cursor / others**: toggle/reconnect the basemind MCP server in the MCP settings.
- **DSH (dsh-basemind-plugin)**: disable and re-enable the `dsh-basemind` plugin row, or restart the
  session. The plugin re-runs its verified binary selection and starts a fresh `basemind serve` on
  the next connection.

rules.find:
posts are never unread for it. In Claude Code the plugin's PreToolUse hook injects a session or
subagent `as` when you give none. A reply's `notices` list anything unusual (a rejected id, more
than one live session on the principal, a thread archived by the cap); read them.
rules.replace:

than one live session on the principal, a thread archived by the cap); read them.

rules.find:
In Claude Code the PreToolUse hook injects `<agent_type>-<8 hex>` when a call has no `as`; that
name is not predictable, so tell any subagent you will address to pass an explicit `as`.
rules.replace:
DSH does not inject `as` (there is no PreToolUse hook), so every call must pass it explicitly —
tell each subagent you address to pass its own `as` on every agent tool call.

rules.find: Build or refresh the basemind index by running `basemind scan` via the CLI. Use this when basemind reports "no index" / "no indexed files", or when `index_status` reports `degraded` or `rescan_needed`. Works without the MCP server — it shells the basemind binary directly.
rules.replace: Build or refresh the basemind index with the `index_rescan` MCP tool, or run `basemind scan` yourself in a terminal (the same version-matched binary as the MCP tools; DSH's `mcp__basemind__cli` tool denies `scan` and `rescan`). Use this when basemind reports "no index" / "no indexed files", or when `index_status` reports `degraded` or `rescan_needed`.

rules.find:
From the repository root:

```sh
basemind scan                   # full working-tree scan
basemind rescan <path>          # re-index only these paths (incremental)
```
rules.replace:
With a live `basemind serve`, rebuild through the MCP tools (the same version-matched binary as the
CLI, no shell, argv only):

```text
index_rescan {}                        # full working-tree scan
index_rescan {"paths": ["<path>"]}     # re-index only these paths (incremental)
```

Without a running server, run `basemind scan` / `basemind rescan <path>` yourself in a terminal
from the repository root — the plugin's CLI tool denies both write verbs.
